query: Can the trial court close prosecution witness cross-examination as 'Nil Opportunity given' when the accused is unrepresented by counsel?
query_text: Can the trial court close prosecution witness cross-examination as 'Nil Opportunity given' when the accused is unrepresented by counsel?

query: Is a revision petition against the dismissal of an application for recall of witnesses under Section 311 CrPC barred as an interlocutory order under Section 397(2) CrPC?
query_text: Is a revision petition against the dismissal of an application for recall of witnesses under Section 311 CrPC barred as an interlocutory order under Section 397(2) CrPC?
target_citations: Ram Swaroop Gupta vs. State NCT of Delhi
expected_ratio: While dismissal of an application under Section 311 CrPC (Section 348 BNSS) is an interlocutory order barring revision under Section 397(2) CrPC (Section 438(2) BNSS), the High Court is justified and duty-bound to invoke its inherent powers under Section 482 CrPC (Section 528 BNSS) where the interlocutory order has resulted in gross injustice to the accused.
ground_truth_answer: While dismissal of an application under Section 311 CrPC (Section 348 BNSS) is an interlocutory order barring revision under Section 397(2) CrPC (Section 438(2) BNSS), the High Court is justified and duty-bound to invoke its inherent powers under Section 482 CrPC (Section 528 BNSS) where the interlocutory order has resulted in gross injustice to the accused.

query: What procedure must High Courts follow for immediate communication and release of prisoners when bail or acquittal orders are pronounced?
query_text: What procedure must High Courts follow for immediate communication and release of prisoners when bail or acquittal orders are pronounced?
target_citations: Pila Pahan vs. State of Jharkhand
expected_ratio: Orders granting bail or acquitting convicts in custody must be communicated to jail authorities and trial courts on the date of pronouncement, and the prisoner must be released on the same day or at most the next day. In urgent matters like habeas corpus or bail, operative orders may be pronounced immediately and reasons uploaded within 7 to 15 days.
ground_truth_answer: Orders granting bail or acquitting convicts in custody must be communicated to jail authorities and trial courts on the date of pronouncement, and the prisoner must be released on the same day or at most the next day. In urgent matters like habeas corpus or bail, operative orders may be pronounced immediately and reasons uploaded within 7 to 15 days.

query: Is a single composite appeal maintainable against a common judgment disposing of both a civil suit and a counterclaim?
query_text: Is a single composite appeal maintainable against a common judgment disposing of both a civil suit and a counterclaim?
target_citations: Basudev & Ors. vs. Sanjay Kumar & Ors.

query: When can an inquiry be dispensed with under Article 311(2) second proviso Clause (c) of the Constitution for an ISRO scientist?
query_text: When can an inquiry be dispensed with under Article 311(2) second proviso Clause (c) of the Constitution for an ISRO scientist?
target_case_title: V R Sanal Kumar vs Union Of India
target_citations: Dr. V.R. Sanal Kumar vs. Union of India
expected_ratio: Under Article 311(2) second proviso clause (c), departmental inquiry can be dispensed with when the President or Governor is satisfied that in the interest of the security of the State it is not expedient to hold such inquiry. The satisfaction is subjective and based on sensitive intelligence that cannot be disclosed or submitted to judicial review unless mala fides are proved.

query: Does unauthorized foreign employment of a space scientist working in rocket propulsion justify summary dismissal on national security grounds?

target_citations: V.R. Sanal Kumar vs. Union of India
